title: Stakeholder Engagement: Quarterly Summary & Renewal Brief
body:
Purpose:
This is a single-file working template for customer-facing quarterly recap emails plus an accompanying one-page executive briefing intended for sponsor-level stakeholders. Goal: make it fast to assemble a polished outreach that summarizes value delivered, surfaces risks/opportunities, and clearly states renewal-related asks and timelines.

Use instructions:
- Personalize the subject, opening paragraph, and 1-2 bullets under "Top wins" with customer-specific metrics.
- Attach the one-page PDF executive brief and the product telemetry snapshot when sending.
- When preparing the sponsor call, use the timed agenda below and bring the "Decision calendar" slide.

Suggested subject lines (pick one, A/B test over 2 cycles):
- "Quarterly recap + renewal timeline: [Customer] & Redwood – Q{n}"
- "[Customer] results this quarter + next steps for renewal"
- "Quick sponsor update: performance, risks, and renewal outlook"

Pre-header (email preview):
4 highlights: latency down 22%, inference cost/unit -8%, 2 new production routes, renewal planning timelines.

Email template (customer-facing recap):
Hi [Sponsor first name],

Thanks for partnering with Redwood this quarter. Quick note to summarize outcomes, risks, and proposed next steps as we approach your renewal window. I’ve attached a one-page briefing for your leadership team.

1) Top wins (2–4 bullets, quant where possible)
- Reduced average gen latency from 170ms to 132ms across priority routes (–22%) through batching + kernel tuning.
- Lowered per-1000-token inference cost by 8% using quantized variant + cache policy on RDW-dedicated pool.
- Integrated customer-specific reranking model for search, improving mean reciprocal rank (MRR) by 0.12 on sample tests.
- Two operational runbooks delivered: incident playbook + prefix cache tuning checklist.

2) Current health snapshot (short bulleted metrics)
- Uptime (SLA routes): 99.93% (rolling 90d)
- Avg latency (p50/p95): 132ms / 480ms
- Token volume (monthly): 82M tokens (increase +14% QoQ)
- Error rate: 0.14% (deploy rollback on 2026-01-18 prevented wider impact)

3) Risks & mitigations (one-line risk, one-line mitigation)
- Spike in peak-hour queueing as usage hits 3x planned bursts — mitigation: enable burst autoscaling and temporary dedicated capacity for top routes.
- Model drift observed on support channels — mitigation: schedule eval run, propose canary for model variant v2.1.

4) Renewal view & ask (clear, dated, and actionable)
- Current contract renewal target: 2026-05-15 (90-day planning window).
- Proposed decision: confirm committed capacity and support tier by 2026-04-01 to lock pricing and SLA.
- Ask for sponsor: identify 1 procurement/finance contact and confirm preferred billing cadence by next check-in (meet by 2026-03-20).

5) Suggested next steps & owners
- Executive sponsor brief and sign-off request (Owner: AM) – prepare summary for leadership meeting by 2026-03-15.
- Technical canary plan for model v2.1 (Owner: Solutions Eng) – schedule canary week 2026-03-22.
- Renewal proposal draft (Owner: CS Rev Ops + AM) – share draft week of 2026-03-29.

Attachments to include when sending email:
- One-page executive brief (PDF) – use the outline below.
- Product telemetry snapshot CSV (tokens, routes, latency hist per route).
- Incident & runbook summary (if applicable).

One-page executive briefing: content outline (single slide / PDF page)
Header: Customer name, Qtr (Q{n} YYYY), Prepared by: Redwood CS (AM name + date)
Left column (visual metrics):
- KPI strip: Uptime | Tokens/mo | Avg latency | Cost/unit (each with current + QoQ delta)
- Small sparkline for tokens and latency trend (last 6 weeks)
Center column (narrative):
- 3-line summary: What we delivered, why it matters to your product goals, headline ROI signal (e.g., time-to-answer down, conversions up).
- Top 3 wins with one-sentence evidence each.
Right column (decision + timeline):
- Renewal calendar: key dates (proposal, leadership review, procurement sign-off, effective date).
- Key ask(s) for sponsor: confirm capacity class, agree audit/KMS details, finalize billing contact.
Bottom strip (risks + mitigations):
- 2-row table: Risk | Mitigation | Impact if unchecked | Owner

Meeting agenda for sponsor check-in (30 minutes recommended)
- 0:00–0:03 — Quick check-in & objective of call (AM)
- 0:03–0:08 — One-page executive brief walkthrough (AM)
- 0:08–0:16 — Deep-dive on a single technical risk or win (Solutions Eng)
- 0:16–0:22 — Renewal timeline + procurement questions (AM/RevOps)
- 0:22–0:27 — Sponsor Q&A and decisions (Sponsor)
- 0:27–0:30 — Next steps & action owner confirmation (AM)

Personalization tips (quick wins)
- Put the sponsor’s business goal in the opening sentence (e.g., "to reduce latency customer-visible by 25%"), not a generic product line.
- Replace "tokens" with customer-native metrics where possible (e.g., "recommendations/sec", "search queries/day").
- Call out any cross-team stakeholders (prod, infra, security) who must be looped into the renewal sign-off.

Decision calendar (example timeline text block to paste into the brief)
- 2026-03-01 — Internal exec review by customer leadership
- 2026-03-15 — Sponsor sign-off on capacity & SLAs
- 2026-03-29 — Redwood sends formal renewal proposal and SOW
- 2026-04-12 — Procurement & legal review complete
- 2026-05-15 — Contract effective date (renewal live)

Escalation & contacts (who to loop if roadblocks arise)
- Primary AM: [AM name, email, phone]
- Solutions Engineering lead: Lena Park (lena@redwood.ai)
- Renewal owner (CS Rev Ops): Daniel Kline (dkline@redwood.ai)
- Executive sponsor escalation: Head of Customer Success, Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai)

Renewal checklist (simple yes/no items to paste into CRM)
- [ ] Confirmed capacity class and expected peak load
- [ ] Security/KMS requirements documented
- [ ] Procurement contact confirmed
- [ ] Proposed SLA/uptimes acceptable or negotiated
- [ ] Renewal decision date set and calendar invite sent

Quick sample closing lines (pick tone)
- Formal: "I appreciate your partnership — we’ll follow up with the proposal and a concise summary for your leadership team by 2026-03-29."
- Casual: "Thanks — excited to keep iterating. Can we lock a quick 20-min slot the week of 3/22 to confirm procurement details?"

Internal notes to AM/SE before send:
- Run the telemetry export for the last 90 days and attach a CSV with per-route p50/p95 and cost breakdown.
- Pull any open incidents in the last quarter and include a 1-line 'status & closure' entry for each.
- Add a short blurb on model evaluation results if proposing a model variant for canary testing.

Version history & author notes:
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft (Priya Nair)
- 2025-12-02: Added decision calendar and sample subject lines (Ethan M.)
- 2026-01-17: Inserted hiring of Lena Park as SE lead and contact updates (Lena Park)
- 2026-02-20: Polished language, added escalation contacts, set status to in_review (Priya N.)

End of template.

Pasteable blocks (for quick assembly)
[PASTE: 1-page brief title]
[PASTE: Top wins — copy 3 bullets]
[PASTE: Snapshot metrics]
[PASTE: Renewal decision calendar]
[PASTE: Next steps & owners]

Notes on confidentiality: This draft is intended for direct customer outreach and contains operational details. Do not publish externally without legal review if it includes contract terms or sensitive telemetry.
